text.p: Grain and oilseed exports reported by USDA and private export sources.

CORN SALES - The Cyprus Grain Commission on Tuesday bought 18,000 tonnes of maize from Cargill Inc at $143.79 per tonne. The price includes C&F, a statement from the commission said. Shipment is scheduled in March.

- Taiwan's CK group bought 108,000 tonnes of U.S. No.2 corn from Mitsui and Co Ltd Tuesday, Taiwanese traders said. Shipment include 54,000 tonnes for April 11-25 from the U.S. Gulf and the balance for April 25-May 9 from the Gulf.

CORN SALES - Korea's Feed Association's office in Pusan bought 74,000 tonnes of Chinese corn on Saturday from Toepfer. It bought 14,000 tonnes at $141.40 a tonne C&F for arrival by May 25 to the port of Pusan. The second and the third, each for 30,000 tonnes, were at $139.90 a tonne C and F for arrival by May 25 and by June 25 to the port of Ulsan.
SOYBEAN SALE - The Taichung division of Taiwan's Breakfast Soybean Procurement Association bought 54,000-tonnes of U.S. soybeans from Bunge Co Tuesday, traders said.

CORN, RICE, CORN/SOY BLEND TENDER - The CCC said it will tender Tuesday for 32,380 tonnes U.S. corn, rice and corn/soy blend for North Korea. It seeks 5,000 tonnes of corn-soy blend, 20,780 yellow corn and 6,600 milled rice. Delivery was for April 1.

CORN AND SOYBEAN TENDER - Taiwan's Hui Shung Group was scheduled to tender Thursday for 38,500 tonnes of U.S. No.2 soybeans and 16,000 tonnes of U.S. No.2 corn, traders said on Tuesday. Shipment for both was slated for April.

SOYMEAL TENDER - South Korean companies on Tuesday were seeking 30,000 tonnes of soymeal for arrival by May 30, traders said. The buyers were aiming to purchase at around $280 a tonne c&f, but may delay the plan due to high market prices hovering over $300 a tonne. Arrival was set for Inchon.

WHEAT TENDERS - Mexico was scheduled to tender by early Wednesday for 29,000 tonnes of U.S. hard red winter wheat, 13.5 percent protein, for April shipment, U.S. exporters said. It seeks 20,000 tonnes to be delivered by ship to the west coast of Mexico and 9,000 tonnes to be delivered by rail.

WHEAT TENDERS - South Korea's Cheil Jedang Corp and Dongah Flour Mills Co Ltd have jointly invited tenders to buy 21,000 tonnes of U.S. wheat by 2:00 p.m. (0500GMT) on Wednesday,traders said on Tuesday.

- The Taiwan Flour Mills Association should tender Thursday for two shipments totalling 69,000 tonnes of U.S. wheat, Taipei traders said. The first shipment is for March 15 to April 5 from the Pacific Northwest (PNW), the second for March 31 to April 20 from the PNW, traders said.

WHEAT TENDERS - The European Union was scheduled to tender February 25 to supply 45,000 tonnes of EU soft wheat as food aid to Bangladesh, France's grain office ONIC said. The EU will hold another tender that day to supply Ivory Coast with 2,480 tonnes of EU maize flour as food aid.
- The CCC seeks 10,500 tonnes US hard red wheat Feb 26 for Bangladesh. It seeks 5,870 tonnes of hard red winter wheat and 4,660 HRW or hard red spring for March 15-April 10 shipment.

MARKET TALK - China bought 950,000 tonnes of soybean meal during the fourth quarter of 1996 compared with zero purchases the year before, U.S. Agriculture Department chief economist Keith Collins said on Monday...USDA Tuesday said it decreased by $5 million the allocation of credit guarantees available for sales of U.S. farm products to the West Caribbean countries of Jamaica and Haiti under a Commodity Credit Corp program for fiscal 1997. USDA said that the decrease lowers the CCC's Export Credit Guarantee Program (GSM-102) for the West Caribbean Region to $35 million.
